chapter_theme: Songs at Devanur (தேவனூர்), all three without a confession about women: the poet asks to pass beyond the counted tattvas and the scriptures into the silence where craving ends, asks to stand praising Murugan's names, and declares Murugan the one reality beyond form, speech, Veda, bindu and nada, turiya and beyond.
structure_note: 734 and 736 are doctrinal; 735 is a plea to praise. 734 and 735 share their closing line.

734.reading: The poet counts off sixes and fives and fours, the constituents of the world, and asks when, beyond these restless things and beyond the art of the Vedas and Agamas, in the great lord whose end cannot be told, without anything else to say, alone and yet all things, he will reach the house of silence beyond the mind, gathered in, with his craving stilled. The praise names the vel that drove back Sura's army over the sea, and Murugan teacher of the lord with matted hair who wears konrai, thumbai, vilva shoots, the young moon, the hissing serpent, karanthai and the river, and the lord who came to shine at Devanur, where all the gods gather.
734.nuance: ஆறும் ஆறும் அஞ்சும் அஞ்சும் ... அறுநாலும்: the counting points to the tattvas, but how the numbers add up is not said and I don't reconstruct it. மனங்கடந்த மோன வீடு and யான் அவா அடங்க: release is a house of silence beyond the mind, reached when the 'I' and its craving are stilled. தேசிகா: Murugan is again Siva's teacher.

735.reading: The poet asks whether he will stand praising Murugan as the friend whom the gods' elephant-reared maid and the hunter girl of the hill desire, as Kanda of the great peacock, until his longing is satisfied. The praise names the vel that uprooted Tarakasura, shook the mountains and set the sea on fire, and Murugan the treasure of the cool lotus-like Lady on the left of the lord with the scars, golden body, Ganga, white skull garland, konrai, thumbai, serpents and arugu, at Devanur.
735.nuance: The plea asks for nothing but the chance to praise: ஆவல் தீர என்று நின்று புகழ்வேனோ. Taraka, Sura's brother, is named here rather than Sura. தழும்பர் is Siva marked with scars, possibly those of Uma's embrace; the text does not say.

736.reading: A song of praise with no plea: the one that cannot be seen, both form and formless, that cannot be spoken yet gives speech, the fullness at the end of the four Vedas, dwelling in the bond of the five-element body, unknown to the illusory body, coming before the embodied and speaking as them, the light in space, unknown to Vishnu and Brahma, growing as the world in difference and non-difference, as bindu and nada, as the knowledge of the kalas, as turiya and beyond it, the fruit of the poet's austerity and the fullness of grace: that one is Murugan. The praise names the vel that crushed the demons and gave their lives to Yama, the child who drank Uma's milk, who struck Brahma on the tuft of his head, the thief who sought the girl on the millet platform, and the lord of Devanur who dwells in the hearts of true jnana-yogis.
736.nuance: The first half is a definition of the Absolute in negatives and pairs (காணொணாதது உருவோடு அருவது, பேசொணாதது உரையே தரவது, பேதாபேதமொடு உலகாய் வளர்வது), ending ஒன்று நீயே, 'the one is you'. Striking Brahma's tuft (குடுமியிலே கரமொடு மோதின) is the punishment for not knowing Om, though Om is not named. காயமானவர் எதிரே அவரென வந்து பேசி may mean the Lord appearing as a human guru.

links.note: Both make silence the door of release: Tirumular says release comes to those to whom silence has come and all speech ends, and 734 asks for the house of silence (மோன வீடு) beyond the mind, where nothing else is spoken.

Tirumular gives form and formlessness and the thirty-six tattvas to Shakti and Siva; 736 gives the same pairs, form and formless, difference and non-difference, bindu and nada, to Murugan and ends 'the one is you'.

736 calls the one that cannot be seen both form and formless (உருவோடு அருவது) and says it comes before the embodied and speaks as one of them (காயமானவர் எதிரே அவரென வந்துபேசி), ending ஒன்று நீயே. Tirumanthiram 2481 says the Lord becomes formless, form and form-formless (அருவாய் உருவாய் அருவுரு வாகி) and comes as guru (குருவாய் வரும்). Both pass from the threefold nature to the Lord appearing as a human teacher; the song says that one is Murugan.
